subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should OpenClaw keep the canonical macOS managed-service PATH, add an explicit opt-in for user bin directories, or include Darwin user dirs by default?
rationale: The code change is straightforward, but the outcome changes a security-sensitive service command-resolution policy that current docs and tests intentionally encode.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep the canonical default and design a documented service PATH opt-in or extraDirs setting with doctor/status guidance and tests.

options.title: Change the default
options.body: Include Darwin user dirs by default and accept the upgrade/security risk that service child processes may resolve tools from user or version-manager directories.

options.title: Keep current policy
options.body: Document that macOS service PATH remains canonical and route user-specific exec tool discovery through tools.exec.pathPrepend, login-shell PATH merging, or explicit command paths.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical default and design a documented service PATH opt-in or extraDirs setting with doctor/status guidance and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current macOS service PATH policy commit and is the clearest owner for deciding whether to change that service boundary.
